code_names: Literacy: Reading and Writing
indicator_names: Grade 3 state English language arts test, percent proficient or advanced; Grades 3-8 state English language arts test, percent proficient or advanced
pathway: Tutoring programs that build children's reading skills raise scores on standardized reading tests, and partner-run versions using trained, paid tutors (including national service members) work too, though effects are smaller at scale.
conditions: Tutoring during the school day by trained, paid tutors (teachers, paraprofessionals or national service members such as AmeriCorps), at least three sessions a week, one-to-one or small groups, using a structured reading curriculum, in kindergarten to grade 3. Volunteer and virtual tutoring count only at the lower sizes below. Homework help or general after-school time does not qualify.
typical_effect: SPARK (Milwaukee) randomized trial: 0.12 standard deviations on a national reading test. A one-year follow-on trial of the same model: significant gains on two reading tests. Education Corps randomized trial: 0.17 at mid-year. Push-in kindergarten tutoring: oral reading 0.23, district reading level 0.11. Paraeducator tutoring in grade 1: better on 5 of 6 tests. Reading Corps: significant gains in kindergarten to grade 3. Recovery-era study: one tutoring program 0.22 and small-group reading 0.33 on state tests. Nashville at scale: 0.04 to 0.09. Volunteer tutoring meta-analysis: 0.23. Virtual tutoring: 0.05 to 0.08 (one-to-one 0.07 to 0.12). Meta-analysis of small-group instruction by adults: about 0.35 to 0.45 on mixed measures. Plan on 0.05 to 0.15 on the state test.
